records.clause_text: An endpoint MAY save the last protected WINDOW_UPDATE frame it receives for each stream and apply the values once the TLS handshake completes.

section_headings: Protected Frames Prior to Handshake Completion

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT use 0-RTT keys to protect anything other than TLS handshake messages.

records.clause_text: Any timestamps present in ACK frames MUST be ignored rather than causing a fatal error.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Protected Frames Prior to Handshake Completion

records.clause_text: WINDOW_UPDATE frames MUST NOT be sent unprotected.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Protocols that use the QUIC transport MUST use Application Layer Protocol Negotiation (ALPN) [RFC7301].
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Servers SHOULD select an application protocol based solely on the information in the ClientHello, not using the QUIC version that the client has selected.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server SHOULD use a HelloRetryRequest if the size of the handshake messages it sends is likely to exceed the size of the ClientHello.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: If the server cannot select a combination of ALPN identifier and QUIC version it MUST abort the connection.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Errors in the TLS connection SHOULD be signaled using TLS alerts on stream 1.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A HelloRetryRequest handshake message and any second ClientHello that is sent in response MUST also be sent without packet protection.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: Implementations MUST NOT exchange data on any stream other than stream 1 without packet protection.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT use 1-RTT protected packets before verifying either the client Finished message or - in the case that the server has chosen to use a pre-shared key - the pre-shared key binder (see Section 4.2.8 of [I-D.ietf-tls-tls13]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a SPLIT alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Similarly, a packet that appears to trigger a key update, but cannot be unprotected successfully MUST be discarded.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An implementation MUST ensure that TLS handshake messages are always sent in cleartext packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Keys and their corresponding secrets SHOULD be discarded when an endpoint has received all packets with sequence numbers lower than the lowest sequence number used for the new key.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once an endpoint successfully receives a packet with a given packet number, it MUST discard all packets with higher packet numbers if they cannot be successfully unprotected with either the same key, or - if there is a key update - the next packet protection key (see [key-update]).
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST treat receipt of an "ACK" frame in an unprotected packet that claims to acknowledge protected packets as a connection error of type OPTIMISTIC_ACK.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST NOT use an "ACK" frame in an unprotected packet to acknowledge packets that were protected by 0-RTT or 1-RTT keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: "MAX_DATA", "MAX_STREAM_DATA", "BLOCKED", "STREAM_BLOCKED", and "MAX_STREAM_ID" frames MUST NOT be sent unprotected.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Updates to Data and Stream Limits

records.clause_text: All "ACK" frames contained in unprotected packets that are received after successful receipt of a packet protected with 1-RTT keys MUST be discarded.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: To limit the number of key phases that could be active, an endpoint MUST NOT initiate a key update while there are any unacknowledged handshake messages, see Section 7.2.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD use data from "ACK" frames carried in unprotected packets or packets protected with 0-RTT keys only during the initial handshake.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Receiving unprotected "STREAM" frames for other streams MUST be treated as a fatal error.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD therefore include acknowledgments for unprotected and any packets protected with 0-RTT keys until it sees an acknowledgment for a packet that is both protected with 1-RTT keys and contains an "ACK" frame.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: TLS handshake messages MUST NOT be protected using QUIC packet protection.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Packet Protection for the TLS Handshake

records.clause_text: Unprotected packets that do not contain a valid integrity check MUST be discarded.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: The integrity check algorithm MAY change for other versions of the protocol.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: For packets other than any unprotected handshake packets (see [cleartext-hs]), once a change of keys has been made, packets with higher packet numbers MUST be sent with the new keying material.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Even though newer keys could be available when retransmitting, retransmissions of these handshake messages MUST be sent in cleartext packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: Like the client, a server MUST send retransmissions of its unprotected handshake messages or acknowledgments for unprotected handshake messages sent by the client in cleartext packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Packet Protection for the TLS Handshake

records.clause_text: An implementation MUST ensure that TLS handshake messages are always sent in cleartext packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST generate ACK frames for these messages and send them in cleartext packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: A server MUST send a TLS HelloRetryRequest in a Server Stateless Retry packet.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A HelloRetryRequest message MUST NOT be split between multiple Server Stateless Retry packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: The extension MAY be included in a NewSessionTicket message.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Any TLS application data or alerts that is received prior to the end of the handshake MUST be treated as a fatal error.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.
section_headings: Denial of Service with Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: Keys and their corresponding secrets SHOULD be discarded when an endpoint has received all packets with sequence numbers lower than the lowest sequence number used for the new key.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Once the TLS handshake is complete, endpoints SHOULD NOT send TLS application data records unless it is to hide the length of QUIC records.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: The certificate that the server uses MUST be considered valid for both connections, which will use different protocol stacks and could use different port numbers.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: All the restrictions on the use of 0-RTT apply, with the exception of the ALPN label, which MUST only change to a label that is explicitly designated as being compatible.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If that validation fails, the server MUST fail the TLS handshake and send an illegal_parameter alert.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A STREAM frame carrying a TLS alert MAY be included in the same packet.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: The CONNECTION_CLOSE frame MAY be sent by either endpoint in a Handshake packet.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: TLS MUST provide integrity protection for address validation token unless the transport guarantees integrity protection by other means.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Upon receipt of a HelloRetryRequest, a client SHOULD cease any transmission of 0-RTT data; 0-RTT data will only be discarded by any server that sends a HelloRetryRequest.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT use protected packets from the client prior to verifying the client Finished message if its response depends on client authentication.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: In order to perform source-address verification before the handshake is complete, PATH_CHALLENGE and PATH_RESPONSE frames MAY be exchanged unprotected.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Clients that receive multiple Retry packets MUST use only one and discard the remainder.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST process ACK frames in unprotected packets until the TLS handshake is reported as complete, or it receives an ACK frame in a protected packet that acknowledges all of its handshake messages.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Retransmission and Acknowledgment of Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: A server that intends to support 0-RTT SHOULD provide an address validation token immediately after completing the TLS handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: To avoid receiving TLS packets that contain no useful data, a TLS implementation MUST reject empty TLS handshake records and any record that is not permitted by the TLS state machine.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Denial of Service with Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: TLS records SHOULD always contain at least one octet of a handshake messages or alert.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once the TLS handshake is complete, both peers MUST ignore unprotected packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Denial of Service with Unprotected Packets

records.clause_text: Unless expressly permitted, receipt of an unprotected message of any kind MUST be treated as a fatal error.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
section_headings: Unprotected Packets Prior to Handshake Completion

records.clause_text: Once the handshake is complete, an error in the TLS connection that causes a TLS alert to be sent or received MUST be treated as a QUIC connection error of type TLS_FATAL_ALERT_GENERATED or TLS_FATAL_ALERT_RECEIVED respectively.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A failure in the handshake MUST be treated as a QUIC connection error of type TLS_HANDSHAKE_FAILED.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Clients MUST NOT attempt to decrypt 0-RTT packets it receives and instead MUST discard them.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: To ensure that this process does not sample the packet number, packet number protection algorithms MUST NOT sample more ciphertext than the minimum expansion of the corresponding AEAD.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: To preserve this separation, a new version of QUIC SHOULD define new labels for key derivation for packet protection key and IV, plus the packet number protection keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Other versions of TLS MUST provide a similar function in order to be used QUIC.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: All other frame types MUST only appear at the 1-RTT levels.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: STREAM frames MUST ONLY appear in the 0-RTT and 1-RTT levels.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: CONNECTION_CLOSE MAY appear in packets of any encryption level other than 0-RTT.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A fatal unsupported_extension alert MUST be sent if this extension is received when the transport is not QUIC.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Packets protected with 1-RTT keys MAY be stored and later decrypted and used once the handshake is complete.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: However, a server MUST NOT process data from incoming 1-RTT protected packets before verifying either the client Finished message or - in the case that the server has chosen to use a pre-shared key - the pre-shared key binder (see Section 4.2.11 of [TLS13]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: After the handshake is complete, endpoints only need to maintain the two latest sets of packet protection keys and MAY discard older keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once this timer expires, an endpoint MUST NOT either accept or generate new packets using those packet protection keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: As it is for other TLS application data, a server MUST treat receiving early data on the TLS connection as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Early data within the TLS connection MUST NOT be used.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate more than one key update at a time.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A client MUST abort a connection if the server picks an incompatible combination of QUIC version and ALPN identifier.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: While there are legitimate uses for some redundant packets, implementations SHOULD track redundant packets and treat excessive volumes of any non-productive packets as indicative of an attack.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT use post-handshake client authentication (see Section 4.6.2 of [TLS13]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: In order to be usable for 0-RTT, TLS MUST provide a NewSessionTicket message that contains the “early_data” extension with a max_early_data_size of 0xffffffff; the amount of data which the client can send in 0-RTT is controlled by the “initial_max_data” transport parameter supplied by the server.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MAY limit the number of keys they retain to two sets for removing packet protection and one set for protecting packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Therefore, an endpoint SHOULD NOT initiate a key update for some time after it has last updated keys; the RECOMMENDED time period is three times the PTO.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Packets with higher packet numbers always use the updated keys and MUST NOT be decrypted with old keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If the packet can be decrypted and authenticated using the updated key and IV, then the keys the endpoint uses for packet protection are also updated. The next packet sent by the endpoint MUST then use the new keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once an endpoint has sent a packet encrypted with a given key phase, it MUST NOT send a packet encrypted with an older key phase.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Because the latter cannot be differentiated from an attack, an endpoint MUST immediately terminate the connection if it detects this condition.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An application-layer protocol MAY restrict the QUIC versions that it can operate over.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: The alert level of all TLS alerts is “fatal”; a TLS stack MUST NOT generate alerts at the “warning” level.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT process data from incoming 1-RTT protected packets before the TLS handshake is complete.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: If the ClientHello spans multiple Initial packets, such servers would need to buffer the first received fragments, which could consume excessive resources if the client’s address has not yet been validated. To avoid this, servers MAY use the Retry feature (see Section 8.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) to only buffer partial ClientHello messages from clients with a validated address.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints that do not have reason to send immediately after completing the handshake MAY send ack-eliciting frames, such as PING, which will cause the handshake to be confirmed when they are acknowledged.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD discard its handshake keys as soon as it has confirmed the handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: PADDING and PING frames MAY appear in packets of any encryption level.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: When multiple packets of different encryption levels need to be sent, endpoints SHOULD use coalesced packets to send them in the same UDP datagram.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: All other frame types MUST only be sent in the 0-RTT and 1-RTT levels.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling application errors (type 0x1d) MUST only be sent in packets at the 1-RTT encryption level.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: CRYPTO frames and CONNECTION_CLOSE frames signaling errors at the QUIC layer (type 0x1c) MAY appear in packets of any encryption level except 0-RTT.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server SHOULD treat the receipt of a TLS ClientHello that with a non-empty legacy_session_id field as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Other cipher suites MUST define usage limits in order to be used with QUIC.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If the number of packets that fail authentication with the same key exceeds a limit that is specific to the AEAD in use, the endpoint MUST stop using those keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: ACK frames MAY appear in any packet number space, but can only acknowledge packets which appeared in that packet number space.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Servers MUST NOT send the "early_data" extension with a max_early_data_size set to any value other than 0xffffffff.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Therefore, the server's use of 1-RTT keys MUST be limited to sending data before the handshake is complete.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: These MUST NOT be used to carry application semantics.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a subsequent key update prior unless it has received an acknowledgment for a packet that was sent protected with keys from the current key phase.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: That is, limits MUST be specified for the number of packets that can be authenticated and for the number packets that can fail authentication.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD retain old read keys for no more than three times the PTO.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Implementations SHOULD use caution in relying on any data which is contained in Initial packets that is not otherwise authenticated.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST count the number of received packets that fail authentication for each set of keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Although it is in principle possible to use this feature for address verification in QUIC, QUIC implementations SHOULD instead use the Retry feature (see Section 8.1 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: If the packet is from a previously installed encryption level, it MUST NOT contain data which extends past the end of previously received data in that flow.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Before a TLS ciphersuite can be used with QUIC, a header protection algorithm MUST be specified for the AEAD used with that ciphersuite.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD retain old keys so that packets sent by its peer prior to receiving the key update can be processed.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A client MAY attempt to send 0-RTT again if it receives a Retry or Version Negotiation packet.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A ciphersuite MUST NOT be negotiated unless a header protection scheme is defined for the ciphersuite.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A client MUST treat receipt of a NewSessionTicket that contains an "early_data" extension with any other value as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Key updates MUST be initiated before usage limits on packet protection keys are exceeded.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once TLS moves to receiving from this encryption level, saved data can be provided to TLS. When providing data from any new encryption level to TLS, if there is data from a previous encryption level that TLS has not consumed, this MUST be treated as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server MAY treat receipt of these frames in 0-RTT packets as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: This Application Data can be replayed by an attacker so it MUST NOT carry a self-contained trigger for any non-idempotent action.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A client otherwise treats 0-RTT keys as equivalent to 1-RTT keys, except that it MUST NOT send ACKs with 0-RTT keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A client MUST only use 0-RTT keys to protect data that is idempotent.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Sending keys MUST be updated before sending an acknowledgement for the packet that was received with updated keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint that receives an acknowledgement that is carried in a packet protected with old keys where any acknowledged packet was protected with newer keys MAY treat that as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MAY perform this process as part of packet processing, but this creates a timing signal that can be used by an attacker to learn when key updates happen and thus the value of the Key Phase bit in certain packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MAY allow a period of approximately the Probe Timeout (PTO; see [QUIC-RECOVERY]) after receiving a packet that uses the new key generation before it creates the next set of packet protection keys.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: When 0-RTT was rejected, a client SHOULD treat receipt of an acknowledgement for a 0-RTT packet as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION, if it is able to detect the condition.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MAY instead defer the creation of the next set of receive packet protection keys until some time after a key update completes, up to three times the PTO; see [old-keys-recv].
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST NOT use 0-RTT keys to protect packets; it uses 1-RTT keys to protect acknowledgements of 0-RTT packets.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: A client MAY consider the handshake to be confirmed when it receives an acknowledgement for a 1-RTT packet.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: If an endpoint detects a second update before it has sent any packets with updated keys containing an acknowledgement for the packet that initiated the key update, it indicates that its peer has updated keys twice without awaiting confirmation. An endpoint MAY treat consecutive key updates as a connection error of type KEY_UPDATE_ERROR.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: The server MUST send a HANDSHAKE_DONE frame as soon as it completes the handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: For the sending of packets, construction and protection of packet payloads and packet numbers MUST be free from side-channels that would reveal the packet number or its encoded size.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Once an endpoint successfully receives a packet with a given packet number, it MUST discard all packets in the same packet number space with higher packet numbers if they cannot be successfully unprotected with either the same key, or - if there is a key update - a subsequent packet protection key; see [key-update].
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: The server MUST treat the inability to select a compatible application protocol as a connection error of type 0x178 (no_application_protocol).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: QUIC extensions MUST describe how replay attacks affect their operation, or prohibit their use in 0-RTT.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: If the recipient of a packet discards packets with duplicate packet numbers without attempting to remove packet protection they could reveal through timing side-channels that the packet number matches a received packet. For authentication to be free from side-channels, the entire process of header protection removal, packet number recovery, and packet protection removal MUST be applied together without timing and other side-channels.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: When using ALPN, endpoints MUST immediately close a connection (see Section 10.2 of [QUIC-TRANSPORT]) with a no_application_protocol TLS alert (QUIC error code 0x178; see [tls-errors]) if an application protocol is not negotiated.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: While waiting for TLS processing to complete, an endpoint SHOULD buffer received packets if they might be processed using keys that aren't yet available.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST initiate a key update ([key-update]) prior to exceeding any limit set for the AEAD that is in use.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST treat the receipt of a TLS KeyUpdate message as a connection error of type 0x10a, equivalent to a fatal TLS alert of unexpected_message; see [tls-errors].
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Once the handshake is confirmed (see [handshake-confirmed]), an endpoint MAY initiate a key update.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Similarly, a client MUST treat the selection of an incompatible application protocol by a server as a connection error of type 0x178.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints responding to an apparent key update MUST NOT generate a timing side-channel signal that might indicate that the Key Phase bit was invalid (see [header-protect-analysis]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Note:: An endpoint MUST NOT reject a ClientHello that offers a cipher suite that it does not support, or it would be impossible to deploy a new cipher suite.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Therefore, a client SHOULD discard 0-RTT keys as soon as it installs 1-RTT keys, since they have no use after that moment.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Clients SHOULD NOT reuse tickets as that allows entities other than the server to correlate connections; see Section C.4 of [TLS13].
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints that limit the size of packets MAY use higher confidentiality and integrity limits; see [aead-analysis] for details.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST NOT initiate a key update prior to having confirmed the handshake ([handshake-confirmed]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: More specifically, servers MUST NOT send post-handshake TLS CertificateRequest messages and clients MUST treat receipt of such messages as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Similarly, a packet that appears to trigger a key update, but cannot be unprotected successfully MUST be discarded.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Though an endpoint might retain older keys, new data MUST be sent at the highest currently-available encryption level.
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST send the quic_transport_parameters extension; endpoints that receive ClientHello or EncryptedExtensions messages without the quic_transport_parameters extension MUST close the connection with an error of type 0x16d (equivalent to a fatal TLS missing_extension alert, see [tls-errors]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST discard its handshake keys when the TLS handshake is confirmed ([handshake-confirmed]).
records.notes: Normative clause later had a MODIFIED alignment; the edit is a review signal, not proof of ambiguity.

records.clause_text: New QUIC versions SHOULD define a new salt value used in calculating initial secrets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Clients MUST NOT offer TLS versions older than 1.3.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If packets from a lower encryption level contain CRYPTO frames, frames that retransmit that data MUST be sent at the same encryption level.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: These updated keys MAY replace the previous keys at that time.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If the total number of received packets that fail authentication within the connection, across all keys, exceeds the integrity limit for the selected AEAD, the endpoint MUST immediately close the connection with a connection error of type AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED and not process any more packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST discard packets that are not long enough to contain a complete sample.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: In addition to counting packets sent, endpoints MUST count the number of received packets that fail authentication during the lifetime of a connection.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Thus, a client MUST discard Initial keys when it first sends a Handshake packet and a server MUST discard Initial keys when it first successfully processes a Handshake packet.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once generated, the next set of packet protection keys SHOULD be retained, even if the packet that was received was subsequently discarded.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A client MUST NOT request the use of the TLS 1.3 compatibility mode.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: When rejecting 0-RTT, a server MUST NOT process any 0-RTT packets, even if it could.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A client MAY wish to apply additional restrictions on what data it sends prior to the completion of the TLS handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: The HKDF-Expand-Label function defined in TLS 1.3 MUST be used for Initial packets even where the TLS versions offered do not include TLS 1.3.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Future analyses and specifications MAY relax confidentiality or integrity limits for an AEAD.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint SHOULD continue to respond to packets that can be processed during this time.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Application protocols MUST either prohibit the use of extensions that carry application semantics in 0-RTT or provide replay mitigation strategies.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A client MUST authenticate the identity of the server.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Future versions of QUIC SHOULD generate a new salt value, thus ensuring that the keys are different for each version of QUIC.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Packets with higher packet numbers MUST be protected with either the same or newer packet protection keys than packets with lower packet numbers.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: After receiving a 1-RTT packet, servers MUST discard 0-RTT keys within a short time; the RECOMMENDED time period is three times the Probe Timeout (PTO, see [QUIC-RECOVERY]).
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If a key update is not possible or integrity limits are reached, the endpoint MUST stop using the connection and only send stateless resets in response to receiving packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Even if it has 1-RTT secrets, a client MUST NOT process incoming 1-RTT protected packets before the TLS handshake is complete.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: The server MAY retain these packets for later decryption in anticipation of receiving a ClientHello.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: For this reason, endpoints MUST be able to retain two sets of packet protection keys for receiving packets: the current and the next.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST NOT send a TLS KeyUpdate message.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Additionally, a server MAY discard 0-RTT keys as soon as it receives a 1-RTT packet.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Any TLS cipher suite that is specified for use with QUIC MUST define limits on the use of the associated AEAD function that preserves margins for confidentiality and integrity.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: First, the packet containing a ClientHello MUST be padded to a minimum size.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: After this period, old read keys and their corresponding secrets SHOULD be discarded.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Servers MAY temporarily retain 0-RTT keys to allow decrypting reordered packets without requiring their contents to be retransmitted with 1-RTT keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Implementations MUST treat any violations of this requirement as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MUST treat receipt of a CRYPTO frame in a 0-RTT packet as a connection error of type PROTOCOL_VIOLATION.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST retain old keys until it has successfully unprotected a packet sent using the new keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MAY refuse a connection if the client is unable to authenticate when requested.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST implement and use the replay protections described in [TLS13], however it is recognized that these protections are imperfect.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: The client therefore MUST reset the state of all streams, including application state bound to those streams.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An application protocol that uses QUIC MUST describe how the protocol uses 0-RTT and the measures that are employed to protect against replay attack.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST NOT send Initial packets after this point.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: It is RECOMMENDED that endpoints immediately close the connection with a connection error of type AEAD_LIMIT_REACHED before reaching a state where key updates are not possible.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Unless another mechanism is used for agreeing on an application protocol, endpoints MUST use ALPN for this purpose.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: An endpoint MUST terminate the connection if a version of TLS older than 1.3 is negotiated.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints SHOULD wait three times the PTO before initiating a key update after receiving an acknowledgment that confirms that the previous key update was received.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A client SHOULD stop sending 0-RTT data if it receives an indication that 0-RTT data has been rejected.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Future header protection variants based on this construction MUST use a PRF to ensure equivalent security guarantees.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: If QUIC needs to retransmit that data, it MUST use the same keys even if TLS has already updated to newer keys.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MAY request that the client authenticate during the handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MUST initiate a key update before sending more protected packets than the confidentiality limit for the selected AEAD permits.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Once a client has installed 1-RTT keys, it MUST NOT send any more 0-RTT packets.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints in either role MUST NOT decrypt 1-RTT packets from their peer prior to completing the handshake.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: Endpoints MAY use a generic error code to avoid possibly exposing confidential information.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.

records.clause_text: A server MAY discard 0-RTT keys earlier if it determines that it has received all 0-RTT packets, which can be done by keeping track of missing packet numbers.
records.notes: Normative text remained identical in at least three document versions; stability is not proof of clarity.
